profile.reading: This is T-Mobile Polskas commercial colocation data center in the Krakow area of southern Polands Malopolska region, opened for commercial use on September 13, 2017 with 400 square meters of colocation space. T-Mobile Poland, part of Deutsche Telekoms international operations, built the facility to meet growing demand for secure enterprise IT infrastructure in the Malopolska region, and the operators own materials describe independent power lines with generator backup, redundant fiber optic routing, fire suppression systems, 24 hour physical security with video monitoring, and a guaranteed 99.99 percent service level. The Krakow site forms part of a wider T-Mobile Poland data center network that also includes two interconnected facilities in Warsaw, known as Szlachecka A and Szlachecka B, linked to Krakow and to a facility in Piaseczno via a dedicated data center interconnect network, allowing customers to combine colocation, cloud, and connectivity services across sites. T-Mobile Poland markets its Polish data center portfolio, including this Krakow facility, to enterprise customers seeking hosting, dedicated servers, private and virtual cloud, and cybersecurity services alongside physical colocation space. T-Mobile Polska traces its roots to Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa, founded in December 1995 and launched commercially in September 1996, which operated for years under the Era brand before rebranding as T-Mobile on June 5, 2011. Deutsche Telekom took full ownership in 2010 after a decade long shareholder dispute with French firm Vivendi, and the company is headquartered in the Sluzewiec district of Warsaw. T-Mobile Polska became the first Polish operator to pass 10 million subscribers by the end of 2005 and reported 13.2 million subscribers and a 30 percent market share by mid 2011, and today runs GSM, 4G LTE, and 5G mobile networks after retiring its 3G UMTS network in April 2023, alongside the enterprise data center and cloud business housed at facilities like this one.
